items.title: ALERT: India's ₹1.28 Lakh Crore Bet on Beating Nvidia's AI Chip Monopoly
items.summary:
India took its first real step toward reducing its dependence on Nvidia. CDAC (Centre for Development of Advanced Computing) has moved its indigenous AI inference chip into trial production, with HCL selected to validate performance across multiple systems and computing architectures.

✅ Cypher 2026: Join 5,000+ AI leaders. Book now → https://cypher.analyticsindiamag.com/tickets
✅ Chess League: Test your skills → https://chess.analyticsindiamag.com/

In this episode of Front Page, we break down what an inference chip actually does versus a training chip, the ₹1.28 lakh crore Semicon 2.0 mission backing this effort, IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnav's 2029-2030 target for a production-grade chip, and why India doesn't need to beat Nvidia globally — just build a domestic alternative for government and critical infrastructure.

items.title: HUGE: Tata's C295 Just Broke India's State-Only Military Aircraft Monopoly
items.summary:
For the first time, a private Indian company has built and flown a full military aircraft, a domain long reserved for state-run giants. Tata Advanced Systems completed India's first made-in-India C295 at its Vadodra facility months ahead of schedule, with the aircraft completing its maiden test flight on June 10.

✅ Cypher 2026: Join 5,000+ AI leaders. Book now → https://cypher.analyticsindiamag.com/tickets
✅ Chess League: Test your skills → https://chess.analyticsindiamag.com/

In this episode of Front Page, we break down the ₹21,935 crore Airbus deal for 56 C295 aircraft, how indigenisation is measured in labour hours and climbs to 98% by the 32nd aircraft, the imported Pratt & Whitney engines and Collins Aerospace avionics still fitted in Vodra, and how the upcoming Dholera airport's MRO facility could set up Tata for civil aircraft manufacturing next.
